SUB gets the highest SecurityGain since arithmetic substitution is cheap, safe, and effective on this integer/float-arithmetic-heavy benchmark. ICALL stays strong (0.8/0.7) to break static call-pattern analysis, with a moderately elevated CorrectnessRisk weight so indirect-call transformation is avoided where types are ambiguous. BCF and FLA carry the heaviest RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights (0.6-0.7) so their application concentrates on cold functions (rInitmatrix, main, Oscar setup) rather than the multiply kernel, accepting them at reduced SecurityGain (0.5-0.6). IBR and SPLIT are mid-to-high across security and diversity with low cost sensitivity, giving cheap structural obfuscation across all 7 functions. IGV is retained at modest weights since this program has few global variables, limiting both its benefit and its risk. Overall the table maximizes layered resistance (arithmetic + control-flow + call + layout transforms) while the cost dimensions keep the compute kernel largely unobfuscated, preserving RealMM's runtime characteristics.
